tier_reason: doc/lamg_plus.tex Table tab:classcomp gives exactly the quoted mean/worst microseconds per nnz for LAMG+, PETSc GAMG, BoomerAMG and others, measured on an Apple M5 Pro; the benchmark code is public (scripts/run_class_comparison.jl, petsc_bench.jl) but no exact Julia version or competitor build flags are stated, and the paper is an author-run arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed, so C.

corrections.caveats: Author-run, first-party; the paper in the repo (doc/lamg_plus.tex, arXiv 2606.24791 preprint) is the evidence. PETSc GAMG is beaten only on some classes: it is faster than LAMG+ on mesh/grid, 3D grid, roads, SPE reservoir and star graphs, and fails to converge on 6 instances. The strongest peer, approxchol_lap (Laplacians.jl), is faster than LAMG+ on social/web/chimera/grid classes; over the 201 graphs with m>1e6 LAMG+ is at parity with it (0.99x geometric mean at 1e-8, 1.20x at 1e-4) and wins on FE/structural matrices (for example bmwcra_1 0.08 vs 0.28 us/nnz). The paper says competitors run in the same Julia process, but scripts/run_class_comparison.jl runs PETSc GAMG (PETSc_jll) and pyAMG in subprocesses and hypre through HYPRE.jl, all prebuilt binaries with unstated build flags. Corpus matrices are not shipped (tens of GB, downloadable from SuiteSparse/SNAP). Commit history shows AI-assistant (Claude) co-authorship on every recent commit.

notes: Every quoted class-table number matches the tex. Repo: Apache-2.0, 0 stars, 49 commits, last commit 2026-07-06, not a fork. Mixed result versus PETSc GAMG: LAMG+ wins 7 of 13 classes, ties FE/structural, and loses 5 (mesh/grid, grid-3D, road, SPE, and star 0.05 vs 0.04).

tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the first-party proxqp_benchmark README numbers match, and the win over OSQP is backed by the peer-reviewed RSS 2022 paper (PROX-QP, Bambade et al.; page itself blocked here, known from search snippet) and by the independent qpbenchmark Maros-Meszaros report (i7-6500U, proxqp 0.6.6 vs osqp 0.6.7.post0), where ProxQP's runtime shifted geometric mean beats OSQP at high (5.9 vs 16.1), mid (19.2 vs 51.9) and low (36.0 vs 52.8) accuracy; no compiler/flags anywhere, so not A.

corrections.caveats: The headline numbers are first-party (proxqp_benchmark, i7-11850H, no compiler, flags or solver versions) and cover the dense ProxQP backend only; the RSS 2022 paper is peer reviewed but could not be opened from this container. The independent qpbenchmark Maros-Meszaros report (i7-6500U, 2024-09-07, proxqp 0.6.6, osqp 0.6.7.post0) is mixed: at default settings ProxQP is slower (runtime shifted geometric mean 53.3 vs OSQP 12.7) but it is faster at high accuracy (5.9 vs 16.1), mid (19.2 vs 51.9) and low accuracy (36.0 vs 52.8), and its success rate is higher (73.2% vs 43.5% at default). Category fit is loose (QP optimization, not linear-system solving) and OSQP is not in the SuiteSparse/Eigen/PETSc list.

notes: All quoted shifted-geometric-mean numbers (18.2, 282.6, 20.4, 3.5, 260.6, 19.3, 14.2, 4.5, 114.2, 108.5, 17.1) appear in the proxqp_benchmark README. Metadata confirmed: BSD-2-Clause, 594 stars, not archived, last commit 2026-09-14. roboticsproceedings.org is egress-blocked.
